summary: The source-derived fix sends underwater coin loss through the same generic dropx/flooreffects route as other lost coins and admits ordinary non-boulder objects on pool or lava terrain. The selected v41 replay now matches all 82 screens and cursors; its first RNG mismatch has moved past apply.c:flip_coin to a later monmove.c:set_apparxy draw during the monster phase after the action. The independent production recipe and recording fully match C across 2541 RNG calls, 55 screens, and 55 cursors.

source.branch: When Underwater is true, flip_coin reports that the coin tumbles away, splits one coin if the stack has more than one, calls dropx, and returns ECMD_TIME without the ordinary coin-face RNG.
callers: apply.c:doapply() dispatches a COIN_CLASS object to flip_coin() at upstream src/apply.c:4241.
apply.c:flip_coin() at upstream src/apply.c:4527-4556 calls do.c:dropx() at src/apply.c:4544; C discards dropx()’s return because it is void.
do.c:dropx() -> dropy() -> dropz() -> flooreffects(); the source flooreffects() pool arm calls water_damage(obj, NULL, FALSE) at upstream src/do.c:315-327 and consumes its ER_DESTROYED result.

JS apply.js:doapply() dispatches to flip_coin(); its underwater arm currently calls note_unported("do.c dropx underwater") at js/apply.js:5171-5174. Existing js/do.js:dropx(), dropz(), and flooreffects() implement the downstream path, but preflight_dropx() currently refuses underwater state and pool landing.

The independent C recipe uses doapply COIN_CLASS dispatch -> flip_coin -> dropx -> dropz -> flooreffects -> water_damage; JavaScript follows js/apply.js:doapply -> flip_coin -> js/do.js:dropx -> dropz -> flooreffects -> js/trap_water_damage.js:water_damage.
dependencies: The existing do.c dropx/dropz/flooreffects JavaScript port and trap.c water_damage implementation are downstream behavior dependencies; this investigation found no competing active reservation for js/apply.js or js/do.js.

evidence: The saved queue entry at .cache/latest-saved-combined-queue.json (SHA-256 7505fb24cd01792c8cb781d651dd66ffaa451361e46f7c456fd2705afde0a43a) identifies batch v41, case v41-underwater-coin-flip-drops-coin, recording challenges/cases/v41/v41-underwater-coin-water-nymph-seven-pages-corrected.session.json (SHA-256 eb1f3e6ac92b42a22c4387ccea87b1bc168e7ba597c68f92035ff4534c48ce79), manifest challenges/manifests/v41.json (SHA-256 7f6627032def2f88334c51f8372f9b61e908665fa995f5d24b06af89532acc69), and evaluation challenges/evaluations/accepted-0acc8a59f86065f8ff2d90ca1decab45701746e8-v41.json at 0acc8a59f86065f8ff2d90ca1decab45701746e8.

At step 81 (key "$"), the C recording calls rn2(20)=5 from trap.c:water_damage line 4771 before the monster action. The original evaluation has 81/82 screens and 2664/2720 RNG matches with 82/82 cursors; the first screen mismatch is the gold total, C 0 versus JavaScript 1.

Fresh run run-zsLkLx of node scripts/diff-fresh.mjs challenges/cases/v41/v41-underwater-coin-water-nymph-seven-pages-corrected.recipe.session.json reproduces the same step-81 boundary: C has 2720 RNG calls and JavaScript has 2675; C’s first call is rn2(20)=5 from trap.c:water_damage:4771 while JavaScript’s next call is rn2(3)=2. Screens are 81/82 with the differing gold count, and cursors are 82/82.

Upstream src/apply.c:4527-4556 establishes that Underwater selects lose_coin, prints “It tumbles away.”, calls dropx(otmp), and returns before the ordinary face-flip draw. Upstream src/do.c:789-797 passes an ordinary non-swallowed drop through dropy/dropz; src/do.c:161-357 handles a pool landing by calling water_damage(obj, NULL, FALSE) and returns whether it was destroyed.

The missing call is explicit in js/apply.js:5171-5174: the underwater lose_coin branch records note_unported("do.c dropx underwater") instead of invoking dropx. The ordinary downstream implementations already exist in js/do.js, but preflight_dropx rejects underwater state at line 1925 and pool terrain at lines 1973-1975. This source trace identifies the needed implementation as removing the underwater coin-flip refusal and admitting ordinary non-boulder objects through the existing pool/lava drop/flooreffects routes without conditioning on coin class or a session coordinate.

After the implementation, fresh run run-IQFe1s on the selected v41 recipe reports 82/82 screens and cursors matching. The first RNG mismatch is call 2665 at monmove.c:set_apparxy:2258 during the subsequent monster phase, after apply.c:flip_coin and trap.c:water_damage have returned. Thus the named flip_coin divergence has moved past the function, while this recording still has a later RNG mismatch.

Independent runtime evidence: recipes/apply.c/flip-coin-underwater-pool-independent.session.json uses seed 41040138, a new date, and a distinct character identity. Its committed C recording matches a fresh differential in run-fXhEQh: 2541/2541 PRNG values, 55/55 screens, 55/55 cursors, and no animation frames. The production input reaches doapply COIN_CLASS dispatch, flip_coin underwater loss, dropx, pool flooreffects, and water_damage.
